::: {.hero-bio}
I am **Emmanuel Hackman**, a PhD student in Computational Science (Mathematics)
at the **University of Southern Mississippi**.

My research develops **physics-informed neural networks (PINNs)** for forward
and inverse problems in partial differential equations: estimating
**dopamine diffusion and uptake** from sparse electrode recordings, and solving
the 3D incompressible **Navier–Stokes equations**, with applications to
Parkinson's disease, fluid dynamics and material science.

## What I am working on

I am building a reproducible research pipeline that benchmarks PINN-based
solvers against classical numerical baselines — projection methods, spectral
solvers, RK4 time integration — on canonical problems such as Taylor–Green,
Kovasznay, and Beltrami flow, and then transfers the validated method to
medical imaging data.

The headline near-term result is a **3D Navier–Stokes PINN validated against
the analytic Beltrami benchmark**, with side-by-side classical baselines on
$L^2$ error, divergence, and wall-clock cost.
See [Research](research/index.qmd) for details.
